idiom_name: project .clang-format (brace style, IndentWidth, ColumnLimit) plus early-return guard clauses
implementation_notes: C++ inherits C's situation and adds named dialects: clang-format ships presets for LLVM, Google, Chromium, Mozilla, WebKit, Microsoft and GNU, so the rectangle is defined by the project's .clang-format (BraceWrapping, IndentWidth, ColumnLimit) and the Core Guidelines ask only that the result be consistent (NL.4: maintain a consistent indentation style). What replaces the Smalltalk bracket corners: one indent step per nesting level, every compound body on its own indented line, braces aligned with the statement that opened them, and preconditions rejected at the top so the normal path stays at one level. The classic hand form is still what you read in C++98-era headers and in projects without a .clang-format; there, match the file rather than reformatting a fragment.
pitfalls: Continuation lines after a wrapped expression or a long call chain are not block indentation; clang-format's ContinuationIndentWidth settings must keep them visibly different from a nesting level, or the rectangle becomes unreadable.
Namespace and access-specifier indentation (NamespaceIndentation, IndentAccessModifiers) are project-wide choices: changing one in .clang-format reformats every file, so decide once.

Templates, lambdas and braced initializer lists mix block and expression shapes; forcing a multi-line lambda into a rectangle hides the fact that it is a value, and a long one belongs in a named function.
